hypothesis: Hydrothermal Permeability Corridor: blind geothermal faults under Quaternary cover are marked not by any single lineament but by the coincidence of (i) dilational jog permeability (stepover / relay-ramp / pull-apart from fault-tip stress) × (ii) hydrothermal alteration (K enrichment, Th/K shift, mag-low halo) × (iii) shallow thermal inertia. Emission is the product field's Poisson-2.8 maxima.
mechanism: At Walker Lane transtensional stepovers, Coulomb failure + tip-crack stress opens fracture permeability; upwelling fluids alter host rock (illite/smectite → K anomaly, magnetite destruction → mag low) and raise thermal inertia. The product of a dilatation proxy (fault-trace curvature × tip distance) and an alteration-thermal proxy (radiometric K/Th + thermal inertia) peaks only where a fault is both permeable and geothermal-active — exactly the geothermal-indicative faults the metric rewards, while single-field lineaments also flag barren bedrock faults.
non_fault_mimic: Alluvial fan apices, lithologic contacts (e.g., basalt caps), and irrigation pivots produce K/mag ridges or thermal edges that can mimic one field but rarely mimic dilational geometry × alteration × thermal together; the product suppresses them. Canary: 500m alluvial-fan apex mask (derived only from slope + 1m LiDAR ex_max, never from labels) — max per-feature AUC 0.7709 ≤0.90 PASS.
